findings.title: Autonomous AI Agents are breaking into hundreds of Online Retailers for $25 a target
findings.summary_md: Gambit Security reconstructed a campaign in which a financially motivated operator used Strix for vulnerability search, Cairn for end-to-end exploitation and Hermes for orchestration against online retailers. Between 10 and 15 September 2026, 105 attack projects were launched and at least 27 companies were compromised to varying degrees, with more than 600,000 credit card records taken. Skimmers were ordered against at least 27 named victims and confirmed on 19 during the campaign, and one retailer's tables were destroyed by the agent's cleanup routine. The article byline is dated 22 September 2026.

findings.title: Path traversal in datastore upload endpoints allows arbitrary file write
findings.summary_md: GitHub advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94 describes a path traversal in MONAI Label's PUT /datastore/image and PUT /datastore/label endpoints, where a caller-controlled image ID is joined to the datastore path without validation and the uploaded file is written outside the intended directory. Authentication is off by default with MONAI_LABEL_AUTH_ENABLE=False, and the ANNOTATOR role is sufficient when authentication is on. The advisory points to pull request 1915 for a fix, says the fix will be in the next release, and recommends enabling authentication, keeping the server off untrusted networks and running it unprivileged with writes confined to the datastore until an upgrade is possible.

findings.title: Chinese-nexus actor's Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own
findings.summary_md: Amazon Threat Intelligence described a Chinese-nexus operator that gave an exposed Cairn instance the single objective of obtaining shell access against universities in East Asia outside mainland China. Agents mapped an open-source medical imaging application's API, found a path traversal in an upload filename parameter in about 11 minutes, and in a later session wrote a Python reverse shell to sitecustomize.py that ran as root. Earlier operations spent about 16 hours and 148 sequential actions on an unauthenticated Redis server and tried more than 30,000 credential combinations built from about 80 harvested usernames, all without success. AWS notified the maintainers, who released a fix and a GitHub Security Advisory, and listed two IP addresses from September 8 to 10 records.

findings.title: China attackers deployed AI agents that autonomously found and exploited a 0-day to take over a university server
findings.summary_md: The Register reported Amazon CISO CJ Moses' account of a China-linked actor using Cairn to find and exploit a zero-day in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging application. It describes the 16-hour, 148-action attempt against an unauthenticated Redis server, failed Log4Shell injection and SSRF against a co-located Qdrant instance, and a separate six-hour credential spray using 80 real usernames from public university sources. The successful run reached arbitrary file write in about 11 minutes and later a root Python reverse shell. The article also cites Gambit Security's report of at least 105 Cairn attacks and compromises at 27 companies.

findings.title: OSV record for CVE-2026-133968
findings.summary_md: The OSV record states that monailabel before 0.8.6 allows directory traversal with resultant remote code execution via the image parameter to PUT /datastore/image. It flags exploitation in the wild starting in September 2026 and records the upstream fix commit associated with tag 0.8.6. The record was published on 20 November 2026.

findings.title: Amazon says Chinese hackers used Cairn AI tool to discover apparent zero-day during attack on university
findings.summary_md: The Record reported that Amazon Threat Intelligence found a publicly accessible Cairn server on 10 September and reconstructed attacks on East Asian universities from its prompts and run history. It quotes the assessment that the path traversal had no assigned advisory and was unpatched at discovery, and that the operator used the same flaw to reach a second university. AWS declined to name the universities or their country. The article places Cairn alongside other autonomous offensive frameworks seen in recent intrusions and quotes Gambit Security's Eyal Sela on the tool's general-purpose design.

findings.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News detailed CVE-2026-133968 as a path traversal in MONAI Label up to and including 0.8.5 in the default no-login configuration, rated 9.8. It reported that the maintainers merged a source fix on 19 October but that the advisory still listed no patched version at publication, and that arbitrary file write could become root code execution through a Python startup file and a training endpoint. The article recommended blocking untrusted access, enabling authentication, running under a limited account and hunting for unexpected Python startup files and unusual training jobs.

findings.title: ThaiCERT: Amazon Finds Attackers Using AI Agents to Autonomously Discover and Exploit a Zero-Day Vulnerability, Gaining Root Access to Servers
findings.summary_md: ThaiCERT summarised Amazon's disclosure of Cairn agents used against East Asian universities, including the roughly 48-hour September campaign, the 16-hour Redis operation with 148 actions, the Qdrant SSRF attempt and the credential spray of more than 30,000 combinations against about 80 usernames. It notes the successful path traversal and root access against a medical imaging system and the proxy tunnel into a second university network. ThaiCERT advises stronger monitoring, investigation of anomalous behaviour and automated detection and response.

findings.title: CVE-2026-133968: MONAI Label Path Traversal Enabling Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
findings.summary_md: Uptycs Threat Research describes CVE-2026-133968 as a CWE-24 path traversal in the image parameter of PUT /datastore/image, with a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8 and active exploitation listed in CISA KEV since 23 November. It identifies MONAI Label versions before 0.8.6 as affected and 0.8.6 as fixed, with a CISA BOD 26-04 due date of 26 November. Recommended actions include upgrading, restricting network access, reviewing outbound connections from the MONAI Label process, isolating confirmed compromises and rotating credentials and SSH keys on affected hosts.

findings.title: MONAI Label Security Update Advisory (CVE-2026-133968)
findings.summary_md: AhnLab ASEC's advisory covers CVE-2026-133968, an arbitrary file write through path traversal affecting MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier. It states that the flaw is patched in MONAI Label 0.8.6 and recommends users update to the latest patched version. The page lists the vulnerability as a security update item for MONAI Label deployments.
